title: Agent payments (Tempo Wallet)
notes: Read 2026-10-21 in a headed Chrome session (the page renders in the browser; a plain HTTP fetch returns the app shell without this text; no Wayback capture). Agents pay over MPP from a stablecoin balance or with MACH, an on-chain credit for payments at approved merchants on Tempo: $1 buys 1 MACH, bought in Wallet through Coinflow, spent by the agent within limits the user approves. MACH does not expire and cannot be sent to another personal wallet, redeemed for cash, swapped or bridged; some services require a stablecoin instead. Legacy MPP Credits remain separate, and buying MACH does not convert them.

title: Tempo docs: Tempo Policy Registry (TIP-403) specification
notes: Read 2026-10-21. The registry lets TIP-20 tokens inherit access-control and compliance policies: simple whitelist and blacklist policies whose admin can update the address set, compound policies with separate sender, recipient and mint-recipient rules, and built-in policies. Tokens check their policy on every transfer, and one policy can serve many tokens. Registry precompile at 0x403c000000000000000000000000000000000000. The page also covers receive policies and blocked-transfer receipts.

title: Stripe docs: Machine payments
notes: Read 2026-10-21 (same text in the Wayback capture of 2026-10-11). Covers MPP and x402. Stablecoin networks: MPP on Tempo (USDC.e) and Solana (USDC), x402 on Base (USDC). Stablecoin payments are available to businesses in all US states except New York, and businesses outside the US can request access in 30+ countries; SPTs are available in all US states. Minimums: 0.50 USD for SPT card payments, 0.01 USDC for stablecoin payments; MPP sessions charge sub-cent increments with a 0.01 USDC minimum settlement. Machine payments work for Connect platforms across all charge types.

title: Stripe docs: Accept streaming payments (MPP sessions)
notes: Labeled Frontier; first Wayback capture 2026-10-01; read 2026-10-21. Uses MPP sessions on Tempo: the agent deposits into escrow, the server charges each unit of work in increments as small as 0.000001 USDC and settles to the Stripe balance in whole-cent increments by creating a PaymentIntent; 0.01 USD is the smallest amount a PaymentIntent can record, and sub-cent remainders are forfeited. The setup enables hostedFeePayer (gasless transactions need a Tempo deposit address on the same account and do not work with Connect).

title: draft-httpauth-payment-01 as posted to the IETF (text)
publisher: IETF (B. Ryan, J. Moxey, T. Meagher, J. Weinstein, S. Kaliski)
notes: Posted 2026-09-09; read 2026-10-21. The recommended HMAC-SHA256 binding uses seven base slots (realm, method, intent, request, expires, digest, opaque) and appends header as an eighth slot when present; the posted text has no test vectors. The repository text at 50309c8 (mpp-specs PR #362, merged 2026-09-21) puts header before opaque and adds three test vectors, and mppx implements the repository order. The two layouts agree when header is absent.

title: wevm/mppx commit b2b1a0b: fix for CVE-2026-34210 in the stripe/charge server
notes: Merge commit of 2026-03-26 that fixed GHSA-8mhj-rffc-rcvw (CVE-2026-34210) in src/stripe/server/Charge.ts: it reads Stripe's Idempotent-Replayed response header and rejects a replayed PaymentIntent with a verification-failed error. In the parent code, the same as tag mppx@0.4.10, both PaymentIntent paths already set the idempotency key to mppx_ followed by the challenge id and the SPT, so a replayed credential got Stripe's cached PaymentIntent back. title: Free-Riding the Agentic Web: A Systematic Security Analysis of x402 Payments (version 2)
notes: Version 2, dated 2026-06-22 by the arXiv API (version 1: 2026-05-29). The v2 full text, read 2026-10-21 at arxiv.org/html/2605.30998v2, names the Machine Payments Protocol among HTTP 402 payment protocols in Section 1, lists the x402, MPP and AP2 exact schemes as candidates for TLA+ or Spin model checking in its future work, and cites the MPP specification; all attacks, measurements and SDK tests target x402. The v1 text does not mention MPP, and neither abstract names it. Four flaw classes: cross-resource substitution, duplicate-settlement race, allowance overdraft and denial of settlement.

title: MPP session method drafts (tempo, evm, hedera, solana, xrpl, lightning) at commit 50309c8
notes: Read 2026-10-21 in the clone at commit 50309c8. Expiry rules by session draft: tempo, evm and hedera channels have no expiry and their vouchers no validity field, and each draft says servers should settle and close channels inactive for about 30 days or more. solana: the server closes a channel after a negotiated idle timeout of 1 second to 30 days, and a voucher can carry an optional expiresAt. xrpl: ledger channels can carry Expiration or CancelAfter, the server must refuse vouchers within a margin of either, and after CancelAfter anyone may delete the channel and the deposit returns to the funder. lightning: sessions have no built-in expiry, and servers should enforce an idle timeout, 5 minutes recommended.

notes: Read 2026-10-21. MAS published a consultation paper on amendments to the Payment Services Act 2019 to implement its stablecoin framework, which it first consulted on in 2022 and finalized on 2023-08-15.
